cells.tense: You're giving and taking in even measure right now, and you know the scale in your hands.
cells.ask: Offer one more than the moment asks for — the extra bit of yourself, freely, where the exchange is already even, and let whatever answers show you what this steadiness is free to hold next.
cells.core:
Somewhere in how you move with people, the accounts run even without you keeping them. What you put in comes back at the same size, what you take you can carry, and nobody ends up smaller for having dealt with you. That evenness is the shape your becoming takes out loud.

The steadiness is built to hold something now. It isn't a truce you're maintaining; it's ground you can stand on while the next thing grows through it. The even exchange is where you're free to give a little past the point of matching, because you're no longer guarding the balance — you're trusting it.
cells.sheetLine: The exchange runs even, and you're the one holding the scale.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair turn, so the exchange stays even between people
cells.place: where you become what you already are

cells.tense: You're bracing for a fairness that hasn't arrived — ahead of the moment, already guarding the exchange that isn't due yet.
cells.ask: Hold one situation without forcing it, once, and let what's yours to carry stay that size — so the strength that contains rather than crushes is what answers the pressure.
cells.core:
You're reading the scales before anyone has put anything on them. Every exchange gets worked out ahead of time — what you'll give, what you'll get, what it'll cost — and the accounting has jumped ahead of the actual living. When you get there, there's nothing left to meet; you already decided how it goes.

What this looks like when it works is simpler than you'd think: you give what's asked, take what's offered, and let the rest sit. The evenness isn't something you enforce from the future. It's what's left when you stop pre-computing and let the giving and taking happen at the speed a person can actually move.
cells.sheetLine: You're balancing a scale before anything's been placed on it.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair turn, so the exchange stays even between people

cells.tense: You keep standing at a fairness that got left behind, and the exchange you're not in is still the one you're measuring against.
cells.ask: Sort one small thing today — one that's really yours to give and one that isn't — and let the time spent telling them apart reconnect you to the people it's been keeping you from.
cells.core:
The exchange stopped somewhere you can't see from here. You're giving less and taking less, and it looks like evenness from the outside, so nobody asks. But you've stepped out of the room where giving and getting happen at all, and standing outside it, you've mistaken your absence for a kind of balance.

This works when you can tell one kind of giving from another — what's yours to offer and what's not, what to take and what to leave — and that's a skill, not a mood. Practicing the sorting is what brings you back into contact. The exchange resumes on its own once you can see it clearly again.
cells.sheetLine: You're matching nobody, and calling it fairness.
cells.verb: Giving and receiving in fair turn, so the exchange stays even between people

cells.tense: You're already giving and receiving in fair measure, and you're describing it like it's happening to you.
cells.ask: Say once, out loud or on paper, that the evenness between you and someone else is something you're choosing — and let that plain fact stand as the knowing you already have.
cells.core:
You're holding the scale in how you deal with people — what you give, what you accept, what you let pass — and it happens automatically enough that you'd say fairness is just what's fair. But the voice deciding is yours, and you've been hearing it as the situation's.

The honest version of this is quiet: you already know what's fair before you talk yourself into calling it something else. When that knowing is trusted — even before you can explain it — the exchanges get simpler, because you're not negotiating with yourself about what you already decided. The fairness is yours. Saying so just brings the title into the room.
cells.sheetLine: You're already doing the fair thing. You just haven't claimed it.
